lumpability_construction: M0/M1 grammar: every request is decided from (i) aggregate per-level book state (M1: projected from the internal shadow engine's anonymous book; M0: the generator-side ledger of the emitted stream alone - the two are cross-checked equal after every accepted submit, so the emitted stream is byte-identical under either feedback_class; asserted by test), (ii) the requesting actor's own unit budgets vs the generator-side ledger (own inventory/cash feedback equivalent under the endowments), (iii) the episode's data-substream RNG / frozen exogenous series

role separation: makers only post non-crossing resting orders (quote-or-join-best rule with spread-gap and level-lockout margins, tainted levels excluded); aggressors only submit walks sized to exactly consumable opposite liquidity, so aggressors never rest and self-trade prevention can never fire

taint discipline: an interior-rationed level is never posted-to and never re-targeted; the next walk on that side sweeps all leading tainted and sub-min_pool levels fully, then targets the first untainted level with R* >= min_pool_units and takes an interior V* in [1, min(R*-1, share_cap)]; every walk-plan pool snapshot therefore consists of intact posted quantities (pure function of the request stream, kernel-invariant)

resource slack: maker cash = band_hi x maker budget, inventory = budget, induced schedule lengths = budgets; per-(actor, side) lifetime posted/walked units capped at the same budgets, so no validation channel (bands, clocks, duplicate ids, cash, inventory, induced capacity, self-trade) can ever fire - zero rejections by construction, asserted against both kernels in tests and enforced in-generator by an ORDER_ACCEPTED assertion plus ledger-vs-engine anonymous-book cross-check after every accepted submit
no cancel/replace/latency-choice requests are emitted (order-id-addressed actions are not M0-admissible per the R2-C grammar clause); request kinds are exactly submit + one terminal finish

kernel-blindness is structural, not statistical: generation consults the shadow engine only through project_anonymous (aggregate totals) and never its RNG; the emitted stream is byte-identical under shadow_rule fifo vs random_unit_within_price (test-asserted on canonical JSON, config fingerprint excluded as it records the knob)

spec_deviations: schema_version pinned 'lab-asset-v3' with arrival clocks carried generator-side only (StreamOrder.arrival_clock + WalkPlan pool clocks), matching the enrichment decision that clocks live in the raw flow, not the prestate; InitialOrder has no arrival_clock field so the prestate cannot carry them. Reason: G3 requires exactly 'lab-asset-v3'; the lab-asset-v3.1 clock enrichment is a fixture-side schema extension.

C4 tick-2x implemented as homogeneous price dilation (reference, half-band, and every generated offset multiplied by tick_factor), so the band width measured in 2-delta ticks is invariant. Reason: the contracts doc pins 'the frozen band-scaling rule' without printing constants; dilation is the unique rule that keeps every price on the coarser lattice with zero per-level distortion, and it is recorded here for D0 ratification.

C4 pop-2x rescaling = actor counts x2 with per-actor unit budgets, induced-value schedule lengths and replenish depth x2. Reason: 'induced capacities rescaled per lab-asset-v3 schema' fixes the schedule-length channel; doubling budgets keeps per-actor slack ratios constant while doubling aggregate activity; recorded for D0 ratification.

No cancel/replace/latency-choice requests exist in the emitted grammar. Reason: R2-C grammar clause - order-id-addressed actions are not M0-admissible unless keyed to aggregate-observable labels, and resting-order survival at rationed levels is kernel-dependent; this is a deliberate class restriction, not an omission.

own cash/inventory feedback is realized inside the generator through per-(actor, side) unit budgets against the stream ledger (exactly executable under the endowments); the engine-side own-state surface is provided as project_own_invariant, tested kernel-invariant, and restricted to aggressors. Reason: makers' own cash/inventory are allocation-dependent (the R2-C off-slack channel), so exposing them to the policy would break the C2(a) class.

M0 and M1 use the same decision rule with different information sources (engine-projected aggregate levels vs generator ledger); because the two sources are cross-checked equal after every accepted submit, the M0 and M1 streams are byte-identical rather than merely law-identical. Reason: this is the R2-C lumpability concession made empirical and is the strongest possible form; recorded as an interface note, not a weakening.

negative_jump_iid is present in D2_SERIES_REGISTRY and D2_NAMED_NOT_RUN and raises ValueError from the canonical entry points (DgpFamily construction / d2_series). Reason: PI decision D1_05 'named-but-not-run'; exclusion is enforced, not merely documented.
The E-2 preflight re-run was NOT executed. Reason: hard rule - it is a separate PI-visible step executed remotely; only the duck-typed compatibility of its evaluation surface is tested locally.
interface_notes: Preflight re-run wiring: import this module as run_preflight's dgp_stream (attribute alias) - build_episode(seed_root, episode_index, cfg_mapping), build_prestate(stream, rule, draw_seed), order_requests(stream), derive_seed(*parts) are signature- and field-compatible with k_preflight_20260906.dgp_stream; verified by running run_episode_evaluations with the alias in tests.

Kernel-swap axis needs no generator change: request streams are kernel-invariant by construction, so the swap replays the same order_requests through build_prestate with allocation_rule exchanged (the replay contract's native operation); shadow_rule is a verification-only knob.

Episode seeds: episode node = SeedSequence spawn_key (data_index, episode_index); the episode's stream rng = child 0, the D2 series seed = child 1; master seed roots for B1/B2 (11000-11029) and B3/B4 (12000-12029) are E-5's to bind; this module never touches init/minibatch/train_kernel/kernel:1..K.

EpisodeStream carries round_id on every submit spec and WalkPlan (round boundaries for E-1's clearing-round grouping are owned by the engine-clock grid, not by round_id; round_id is metadata only, matching E-1's convention).
config_fingerprint(cfg) is the manifest binding surface for the D0 freeze (hash of the canonical config JSON); episode_canonical_json is the byte-identity surface for G8/G9-class determinism checks.

Feedback semantics for the prereg's M1 own-state question (C2(e) rewrite): the generator's own-state structure is budget-ledger-based with the engine-side aggressor own-state projector provided; the preflight re-run measures this actual generator.
